paragraphs: Ravina the Later, Rav Ashi's pupil-colleague: Eruvin 63a. Beitzah 6a: he sat before Rav Ashi and asked, “Why does the master not set aside the eruv today?” Ravina called Rav Ashi ‘master,’ since he was his pupil-colleague (Shittah Mekubbetzet). His place was Mata Mehasya: Rashi, Yoma 86a. Rav Ashi likewise headed the academy there (see there). Ravina and Rav Ashi were the end of authoritative teaching. A mnemonic: ‘Until I come to the sanctuaries of God’ hints at Rav Ashi; ‘I shall understand’—avinah—signifies Ravina; ‘their end’ signifies the end of the amoraim: Bava Metzia, Ha-Po'alim. Tzemah David, 4234, writes that Ravina was the end of the amoraim, and that Halikhot Olam and Yuhasin gave the mnemonic “I shall understand their end.” He forgot that this mnemonic is in the Gemara, Ha-Po'alim. Heilprin quotes Rav Sherira Gaon as writing in Yuhasin: “On Sunday, 13 Kislev, year 811” (AM 4259, with cross-references to 4181 and 4234 in Part I), “Rabbana Avina son of Rav Huna, namely Ravina, died, and he was the end of authoritative teaching.” The checked Epistle and Heilprin’s Part I entry for AM 4234 give Wednesday. Heilprin quotes Ravina here as saying, “Whoever loves to learn in a group.” Makkot 10a and Heilprin’s Introduction give “to teach” for Ravina and “to learn” for Rav Ashi. See the introductory Rules. See there whether Rav Ashi was older than him or the reverse. Ravina said, ‘My mother told me: your father acted according to R' Hiyya’: Berakhot 39, beginning of b. “Your father did not eat new grain until the evening after the seventeenth, as the eighteenth began” (Menahot 68b). Yuhasin writes: Ravina's father, in Rav Yosef's name and Rav Pappi's name (see Marimar). He arranged a match for his son in Rav Hanina's household, etc.; he told him, ‘Does the master not accept Rava's statement?’ (see there). Ravina sat before Rav Assi—it should read Ashi, as in Rashi. He saw him—Ravina saw Rav Ashi—looking sad and asked, ‘Why is the master sad?’ etc.; ‘Did not Rava say?’ Beitzah 6a. Ravina stood behind Rav Ashi and spat backward. Rav Ashi asked whether he accepted the statement about absorbing it into a scarf. Ravina replied, “I am sensitive.” The passage is at Berakhot 24b, cited here as 25b. The checked text names Rav Yehudah. He asked Rav Ashi, ‘Does the master not accept Rav Hillel's statement?’ Some say, ‘Rava's statement’: Shabbat 109a. He died before Rav Ashi: Mo'ed Katan 25b, where Rav Ashi asked the eulogist what he said in Ravina's eulogy (see Rashi there). The halakhah follows him against Rav Aha and Rav Ashi (see there).

Since there is an unqualified Ravina the Earlier and an unqualified Ravina the Later, I have arranged the notices so that you can discern by the generations whose teacher, pupil, or colleague belonged to the earlier or the later one.
